title: How I Choose
pitch: How I Choose is a local-first rehearsal workspace that checks whether a communication partner followed a person's self-authored protocol-never evaluating the person.
about_excerpt: How I Choose is a local-first rehearsal workspace that checks whether a communication partner followed a person's self-authored protocol-never evaluating the person. Like Comment Story Updates Inspiration Important conversations often become harder when speech, language, or processing gets difficult. Yet many communication tools still ask the person to perform better: answer faster, choose from someone else's categories, or fit a fixed conversational rhythm. We wanted to reverse that responsibility. How I Choose asks whether the communication partner adapted to the person—not whether the person performed correctly. The person defines what helps, what each signal means, how much time is needed, and what a partner must do next. The software turns those choices into a protocol that can be rehearsed and audited without inferring meaning from silence or delay. What it does How I Choose is a local-first communication rehearsal workspace for adults. A person authors their preferred channels, wording, pace, processing time, literal-language rules, semantic signals, and partner actions. They also choose exactly which fields an active browser agent may read. The workspace supports both human-only practice and an optional WebMCP agent rehearsal. Before any partner turn becomes visible, a deterministic engine checks it against the current protocol. It enforces one question at a time, word and option limits, channel rules, pending-signal acknowledgment, Pause, terminal Stop, revision freshness, conflicts, and idempotency. The person directly selects every semantic signal, including yes, no, not sure, more information, more time, rephrase, Pause, and Stop. Silence creates no event and never advances the rehearsal. Reports contain evidence about the partner's adherence and repairs ; they never score the person. The complete human-facing product includes: guided onboarding plus blank and clearly labeled synthetic profiles; profile, signal, and per-field agent-access editing; a large keyboard-accessible signal board; low-stakes rehearsal templates and partner-turn validation; partner-adherence audit and revision history; staged protocol suggestions with exact diffs and provenance; JSON import/export and a printable support guide; visible owner-only review and ratification; text-size, contrast, Quiet, and Plain language preferences. Why WebMCP This workflow needs an agent to operate inside the person's current, visible, revisioned protocol , not inside a detached chat containing copied instructions. WebMCP lets ChatGPT use the page's existing permissions, validator, state machine, and evidence while the person retains direct control of signals, rule changes, and approval. The workspace starts in Human-only mode. All eight Site tools fail closed until the person visibly enables Agent rehearsal. Once enabled, ChatGPT can read only allowlisted fields, audit readiness, start an already approved scenario, offer a validated partner turn, acknowledge the exact person-selected signal, inspect its own adherence, stage a draft improvement, and verify guide derivation. There is deliberately no tool for selecting a person's signal, answering for them, resuming, ratifying, publishing, sharing, exporting private data, deleting a profile, or assessing capacity, consent, diagnosis, comprehension, safety, or coercion. How we built it The app is a static Next.js and React application written in strict TypeScript. Dexie/IndexedDB is the durable local source of truth; Zustand holds hydrated read projections and transient preferences. Zod validates every persisted document, import, command, and Site-tool payload. Human controls and WebMCP handlers use the same application-service command path and pure domain logic. Compare-and-swap revisions, idempotency fingerprints, events, and state writes happen atomically in one IndexedDB transaction. Ratified profile snapshots are immutable and identified by canonical hashes. The top-level /demo/ page feature-detects WebMCP and imperatively registers a stable catalog through document.modelContext.registerTool() : get_rehearsal_brief audit_rehearsal_readiness start_approved_rehearsal offer_partner_turn read_latest_signal get_rehearsal_report stage_protocol_patch verify_support_guide A singleton guard prevents duplicate registration under React Strict Mode. Every JSON Schema is bounded and closed with additionalProperties: false , then Zod validates again at the application boundary. Mutations require expected revisions and an idempotency key. Handlers resolve current IndexedDB state at invocation time instead of trusting stale UI state. The quality system combines Vitest, Testing Library, fast-check property tests, Playwright desktop and narrow-viewport suites, axe-core checks, dependency and secret audits, a static production build, and GitHub Actions. The release includes 76 unit, service, property, import/export, and agent-flow tests plus a complete 15-step browser judge path. Challenges we faced Treating discovery and authorization as separate problems. Registering a tool successfully does not mean it should be authorized in the current state. A real-browser test exposed an early version where Human-only was only presentation state. We fixed this by making owner-controlled agent access durable, revisioned session state and enforcing it inside every handler. Keeping agent authority physically narrow. Removing dangerous fields from a broad object was not enough. We created allowlisted agent DTOs and a separate AgentRehearsalService that cannot import owner-only ratification, signal selection, export, share, delete, or resume operations. Making concurrent changes recoverable. A person may change a rule while an agent is preparing a turn. Expected revisions cause the stale write to fail instead of overwriting the person's newer choice; the agent can reread the brief and adapt. Building safety without making clinical claims. The product is deliberately scoped to synthetic and low-stakes adult communication practice. It does not infer answers, assess a person, or present itself as a consent system, medical device, emergency plan, or legal instrument. Accomplishments that we're proud of One deterministic engine governs both human and agent partner turns. Human-only access fails closed, while owner-enabled agent access remains field-scoped and revisioned. Pause is immediately effective and Stop is terminal—no agent override exists. Stale revisions, duplicate requests, invalid turns, repair, signals, and provenance are visible and recoverable. Private notes are structurally absent from agent projections, and receipts contain metadata rather than authored conversation text. The full human product works without an account, backend, API key, remote database, analytics, or runtime external model call. The deployed production build was exercised in ChatGPT's real built-in browser: all eight tools were discovered and the guarded workflow, including Human-only denial and visible
video_transcript_excerpt: Most communication tools ask whether the person performed correctly. How I choose asks a different question. Did the partner adapt? It is a local first rehearsal workspace built around the person's signals, pace, and words. This synthetic profile belongs to Maya. She asks for text first, one short literal question, no more than two options, and explicit handling of every signal. The protocol is visible, editable, and versioned. Agent access is never assumed. Human only blocks every site tool until the person enables agent rehearsal. Even then, the agent receives only exposed fields. It cannot answer, select a signal, resume, ratify, publish, share, or export. The guardrails do real work. A long two-question turn is rejected before it can appear. The result names both failures. Too many questions and a breached word limit. A repaired one-question turn passes the same engine used by human only practice. Only then does the question appear in the practice room. Maya herself selects a semantic signal. When she chooses amber, the system records exactly "Not sure." The partner must acknowledge it and rephrase without changing the choice's meaning. Maya can change her protocol during rehearsal. A stale write is rejected instead of overriding her decision. After reading the new revision, the partner adapts to text only. The red stop signal is immediate and terminal. Further turns are blocked. Silence and delay never create an answer, agreement, or permission. The audit evaluates partner adherence only. Violations, repairs, signal acknowledgement, revision recovery, and stop honored. It never scores the person's comprehension, capacity, consistency, emotion, diagnosis, or consent. An agent may stage a provenance linked improvement, but every change stays a draft until the person reviews it. The support guide is checked against accepted rules. Ratification is a visible owner workflow, never a site tool. How I choose is open alpha communication practice, not a consent system.

live_observation.first_impression: An accessibility-oriented workspace explains partner adaptation and offers synthetic demo or blank-profile entry points plus practice/audit navigation.
live_observation.after_state: The page remained on the landing view with no visible transition or changed state.
live_observation.notes: The stated protocol/rehearsal purpose is clear, but the synthetic-demo action showed no observable response.
